where: Section 3 and Worked example 1, steps 4–5 (also quiz Q4)
problem: Section 3 says that with pipelining the stages overlap and the rate is set by the slowest stage instead of the sum, and the exam traps repeat that pipelining raises the frame rate without shortening latency. But step 4 then computes the highest sustained rate as 1000 ÷ T, where T is the whole 12 ms chain, and step 5 says the system can only hold 83.3 frames per second. The two rules contradict each other, and Q4's answer (ten ms chain, 100 frames per second) repeats the contradiction. A student cannot tell which rule to apply.
fix: State that f_max = 1000 ÷ T is the sustained rate only when the four stages run one after another with no overlap. Add the overlapping case: when the stages are pipelined, the display can be fed once every slowest-stage time — here the GPU's 5 ms, so up to 200 Hz — while each image is still 12 ms old. At 90 Hz the panel can therefore be fed on time, and the cost appears as about 12 ms of lag rather than as a fall to 83.3 frames per second. Give Q4's answer the same two-part treatment.

problem: The note defines f twice: once as 'the display refresh rate in hertz' and again as 'f is frames per second'. A student may think these are two different quantities and look for two symbols.
fix: Write it once: 'f is the display refresh rate in hertz, which is the same number as frames per second'.

problem: 'the GPU shades thousands of pixels per pass' clashes with Section 1, which says the GPU works over millions of pixels. A frame shades millions of pixels; only one pass works on thousands at a time.
fix: 'the GPU shades millions of pixels per frame, thousands at a time per pass, or splits the screen into tiles'.
